step_0_rd_template_convention.question: Does {{rd|8%|5%}} mean melee 8% / ranged 5%, or the reverse?
step_0_rd_template_convention.method: Surveyed every {{rd|...}} usage in data/items.json and cross-checked against effects whose melee/ranged split is stated in the item's own text.
step_0_rd_template_convention.evidence: Tiamat and Ravenous Hydra: {{rd|40% AD|20% AD}} (cleave is 40% AD melee, 20% ranged). Titanic Hydra: {{rd|1%|{{fd|0.5}}}} and {{rd|4%|2%}}. Hullbreaker: {{rd|120%|{{ap|120*0.7}}}} i.e. ranged = 0.7x melee. In every case the FIRST argument is the melee value.
step_0_rd_template_convention.conclusion: {{rd|A|B}} = melee A / ranged B. Jax is melee, so Expose Weakness = 8% increased damage taken.

step_1_target_stats_level_18.independent_confirmation: The committed record reports the subject enemy:Aatrox with max_health 2588 and ending_health 2588 (death_time null). My from-scratch 2588.0 reproduces max_health exactly, confirming the scenario parameters and the growth formula application.

step_2_attacker_stats.jax_ap: 0 (neither Black Cleaver nor Bloodsong grants abilityPower; both stats blocks are 0.0)

step_3_bloodsong_spellblade_line_type_an.type: PHYSICAL, stated twice and unambiguously: wiki branch says "{{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]"; riotDescription tags it <physicalDamage>.
step_3_bloodsong_spellblade_line_type_an.agreement: 73.47 vs 73.2 = 0.4% residual, well inside the documented +/-20% envelope of the 0.8*max_stacks constant. The spellblade line is confirmed physical AND confirmed to be modelled at ~100% base AD through armor.
step_3_bloodsong_spellblade_line_type_an.amp_not_folded_in: If the 8% Expose Weakness amplifier were folded into the spellblade instance itself, the spellblade row would read 73.47 * 1.08 = 79.35. It reads 73.2. Therefore the engine authors the Expose Weakness amplification as SEPARATE attribution rows rather than inflating each damage instance. That is exactly what the two expose_weakness_Bloodsong rows at t=7.5 are.

step_4_magic_side_cross_check.jax_w_empower_rank5: Additional Magic Damage 190 (+60% AP; AP=0) = 190 raw magic
step_4_magic_side_cross_check.agreement: 113.87 vs 113.8 -> 0.06%. Confirms MR 66.85, zero magic penetration, and that the fight carries a substantial MAGIC damage stream alongside the physical one.

step_5_the_typing_argument_that_decides_.premise_a: Expose Weakness is NOT a damage line. Its wiki text grants no damage of its own: it makes the target "take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage FROM ALL SOURCES for 4 seconds". It is a vulnerability/amplification debuff.
step_5_the_typing_argument_that_decides_.premise_b: An amplifier of 'all sources' has no intrinsic damage type. Any row that attributes amplification must inherit the type of the damage instance it amplified.
step_5_the_typing_argument_that_decides_.premise_c: This scenario's damage stream is genuinely two-typed. PHYSICAL: Jax auto attacks, Jax Q Leap Strike (65-225 + 100% bonus AD, tagged Physical Damage), and the Bloodsong spellblade proc itself. MAGIC: Jax W Empower additional magic damage, Jax E Counter Strike magic damage, Jax R on-hit magic damage, and ally Lulu's Q (recorded as magic at [78]).
step_5_the_typing_argument_that_decides_.conclusion: Because Expose Weakness amplifies both streams, a correct attribution requires exactly TWO expose_weakness_Bloodsong rows at the application instant: one PHYSICAL and one MAGIC. A single-typed Expose Weakness row would necessarily misattribute one of the two streams. The committed pre-change record does precisely this: [82] physical (pair 98.6) and [83] magic (pair 170.2), both at t=7.5, sequences 34 and 35, immediately after the spellblade row at seq 33 that applied the debuff.
step_5_the_typing_argument_that_decides_.so_the_subject_event: main:enemy:Aatrox:33 is the PHYSICAL member of that pair. 'physical' is the correct damage_type for this event.
step_5_the_typing_argument_that_decides_.magnitude_consistency_note: Reading pair_damage as the amplified share at the melee rate: physical base = 98.6/0.08 = 1232.5, magic base = 170.2/0.08 = 2127.5. The physical figure is the right order for Jax's physical output to 6.85s (mitigated auto 180.25*0.52385 = 94.4 each, ~7-9 autos, plus Q ~139 mitigated, plus spellblade 73.2 -> ~900-1100), whereas the ranged rate would demand 98.6/0.05 = 1972 physical, which Jax cannot produce in this window. This corroborates melee 8%. It is offered as corroboration only: pair_damage semantics is engine bookkeeping (at [78] pair 119.8 exceeds raw 100.0), and magnitude is not the adjudicated leaf.

step_6_where_the_new_value_actually_come.observation: The pre-change record at index [84] is main:enemy:Aatrox:35 — attacker main, t=9.5, sequence 7, source "E", damage_type MAGIC, skipped_reason "outside_window".
step_6_where_the_new_value_actually_come.arithmetic: S6/S7 removed two events from this 85-record list at positions at or before 82. Removing two members shifts old[84] into new[82]. old[84].damage_type = "magic" and old[84].sequence = 7 — which are EXACTLY the two 'new values' offered in the brief for both leaves of this cluster.
step_6_where_the_new_value_actually_come.inference: The pairing 'physical -> magic' is not a change to the subject event. It is a comparison of the subject event against the Jax E cast that slid into ordinal 82. Both leaves of this cluster are one reading of the same ordinal substitution.

decidability_statement: damage_type IS decidable from the permitted evidence. The Bloodsong Spellblade line is stated as bonus PHYSICAL damage on-hit in both the wiki branch text and the Riot description; Expose Weakness carries no type of its own and inherits the type of what it amplifies; this fight amplifies both a physical and a magic stream, so a physical Expose Weakness row is required and correct.
verdict_reasoning: Against the event identified as main:enemy:Aatrox:33 — the physical member of the t=7.5 Expose Weakness pair — the pre-change value 'physical' is correct on the cached wiki text. The proposed 'magic' is not a reading of this event at all: it is the damage_type of a different record (the Jax E cast, old index [84], seq 7, magic) that occupies ordinal 82 after two earlier members were removed. Even under the hypothesis that this very record was itself removed by S6/S7, a removal is a membership transition and not a value change, so 'magic' still is not this event's damage_type.

supersedes_prior_brief_defect.defect: R-18 addressed this leaf purely by ordinal (/combat/events[82]/damage_type) with no event identity — no event_id, no timestamp, no source, no list length — and withheld the tree that would expose the substitution. Because S6/S7 removed two earlier events from cleaver_bloodsong_roster, leaf_report paired the OLD snapshot's events[82] with the NEW snapshot's events[82] although they are different events, so 'physical -> magic' compared a Bloodsong expose/spellblade proc against a Jax E cast. The posed question had no single referent and no verdict issued against it could be a verdict about one event.
supersedes_prior_brief_defect.remedy_applied_here: This re-adjudication addresses the record by event_id main:enemy:Aatrox:33 and carries the R-15/R-18 amendment's timestamp/ordinal/trigger-context clause: t=7.5, sequence 34, source expose_weakness_Bloodsong, neighbours [81] spellblade seq 33 physical and [83] expose_weakness seq 35 magic. The adjacency of two same-source rows differing only in damage_type is precisely what the ordinal-addressed brief destroyed, and it is what makes the typing question answerable.

unmoved_sibling_facts_confirmed: damage 0.0 and raw_damage 0.0 with pair_damage 98.6 and skipped_reason 'attacker_dead' are internally consistent: the holder `main` (Jax) dies at 6.85 while the event is authored at 7.5, so the row is authored-but-not-dealt. The subject enemy:Aatrox therefore ends at ending_health 2588 of max_health 2588 — which my independent growth-formula computation reproduces exactly (650 + 114*17 = 2588.0). None of this bears on the damage TYPE of the authored row, which is fixed by the item text.
